title: Revisit: does orcasite need polymorphic item_tags for detection review?
description: Opened 2026-08-14 by dthaler on orcasite#1017: 'it's important for the orcasite database and moderator UI to have this functionality or we won't be able to move off the other moderator UI.' Consolidating on orcasite as the single moderation UI (confirmed 2026-08-13) means orcasite must absorb OrcaHello's detection review — and a human confirming or rejecting a detection is a human determination ON a detection, which orcasite cannot currently record. My earlier position (tags stay bout-only; machine class is a field on the detection) holds for MACHINE assertions but does not cover this. ItemTag's ItemTagItem calculation already anticipates it: 'Update constraints/output to Union type once we have other taggable items.' Two distinct things attach to a detection — model assertion and human determination — and keeping them apart is the design. Asked dthaler what else the OrcaHello moderator UI does that orcasite would need to cover; only the detection review path has been read.
notes:
Context on TagHierarchy: dthaler authored it 2026-07-31 in orcahello#561, because 'moderators have been leaving the tags field blank because it was time consuming to fill it in' — independent confirmation of the affordance principle salish-8vr.9 / orcasite#1015 rests on. pigu resolves already (SSA:0000909 Cepphus columba carries PIGU as a hidden name); kier was a typo for keir, fixed in orcahello#573 (see salish-8vr.21 / salish-8vr.23 for KEIR verification).
ANSWERED 2026-08-19 — dthaler listed what the OrcaHello moderator UI does that orcasite would need to cover (not necessarily complete):
- orcasite#953: SRKW yes / no / UNSURE — moderated tags do yes/no but not 'unsure', so a separate property
- a per-detection 'moderated' boolean (or anything isomorphic) is REQUIRED — without it seeded predictions and human determinations are indistinguishable
- spectrogram showing which segments of the clip have calls, with jump-to
- shows who reported the candidate (PODS-AI vs OrcaHello)
- shows how many segments had calls + overall machine confidence %
- free-form labels beyond the preset hierarchy
- 1-click add/remove of labels (no typing in typical cases)
- two-factor auth
- separate views for unmoderated vs confirmed / false-positive / moderated-as-unknown
orcasite#935 is the umbrella for discrepancies.
Also 2026-08-19: dthaler REJECTS 'tags stay bout-only' as an end state — 3-second-granularity moderator tags are desirable (Tong's ask); Dave Bain says only that it is too much moderator work today. And OrcaHello stores per-3s-segment predictions orcasite lacks — a DB-merge blocker.
The answer to this bead's question may depend on salish-8vr.22 (which UI is the end state).
ATTRIBUTION ASYMMETRY (verified in code 2026-08-19): OrcaHello attributes review per-DETECTION, not per-tag — one Moderator (AzureAD UPN) + one Moderated timestamp on the detection document, and DetectionsController.cs:486 overwrites metadata.moderator on every save (last writer wins, no history). With PODS-AI seeding Tags, a saved review attributes the WHOLE tag set to that moderator — actively-confirmed vs passively-left-seeded is indistinguishable per tag. orcasite is strictly richer: item_tags.user_id with identity (user_id, tag_id, bout_id) — per-tag, per-user rows; two moderators can independently apply the same tag; destroy limited to own rows (server/lib/orcasite/radio/item_tag.ex). Implication: 'moderated boolean or isomorphic' is the FLOOR (all OrcaHello can offer); per-tag/per-user attribution is what actually keeps a model's seed distinguishable from a human's confirmation. Migration one-way door: historical OrcaHello tags can only arrive as 'attributed to the detection's last moderator, per-tag confirmation unknown.'
DESIGN CANDIDATE 2026-08-19 (rainhead): taggings as EVENTS. Append-only {actor (human user | model+version), item, register identifier, stance (present/absent/unsure), certainty/confidence, time-scope, timestamp}; current tag set is a fold. Dissolves in one shape: seeded-vs-confirmed (actor kind), the 'moderated' boolean (derived: any human event exists), #953 yes/no/unsure (stance), bout vs detection vs 3s-segment (time-scope on the event, not a schema fork), attribution (one actor per event), and OrcaHello's hand-rolled 'originals remembered for model improvement' (natural log property). Reframes the epic's separation principle: model assertion vs human determination kept apart by ACTOR KIND within one shape rather than by table. Precedent: iNaturalist identifications (append-only per-user, withdrawal not deletion, community taxon = fold); DwC Identification class consumes an event stream naturally; decision 013 gets easier. Costs: fold semantics are real design work (does human supersede model? is removal a retraction event?); bigger upstream ask than a column while elixir cycles are scarce (salish-8vr.22) — though item_tags is already close (per-user rows + timestamps; delta ≈ never hard-delete, add stance + actor-kind); OrcaHello history still arrives coarse (one event per detection, last moderator). Raise at the meeting alongside .22.

title: Reconcile normalize_designation() with the register's fold (ADR-0019)
description: ADR-0019 publishes the fold as THE matching rule and names our normalize_designation() as the thing to reconcile. Two divergences: (1) direction — ours pads (T65A5 -> T065A5) where the fold strips leading zeros (T090 -> t90); same goal, opposite convention, and only one can be the shared rule. (2) The trailing 's'. ADR-0019 refuses to fold it because T090s names the matriline and T090 its matriarch — 126 pairs depend on staying apart. supabase/migrations/20260708000104_identifier_candidate_cache.sql:41 strips 's$' before matching against grp.designation; verify whether that survives into matching, which ADR-0019 says it must not. Ours also does not handle apostrophes or hyphens at all. Acceptance: our implementation reproduces dist/fold_test.tsv exactly (a scratch Python version already does, so the rule is cheap — the question is what changes in SQL and what it breaks). Interacts with finding F9 in docs/design-notes/occurrence-identification-findings.md, which proposed searchable_name.tsv as the lookup table; ADR-0019 supersedes that with a rule instead of rows.

title: Link native and iNaturalist contributor records for the same person
description:
A person who observes through both SalishSea.io and iNaturalist has two contributors rows with nothing connecting them. inat_login is a dedup key for iNat rows only (D-15: native rows leave it NULL) and it is UNIQUE, so a native row cannot even be tagged with a login an iNat row already holds.

This is what blocks 'source the ORCID from iNaturalist where possible' from being machinery rather than a curation habit: the ORCIDs we hold sit on iNat rows, the archive exports native rows, and nothing joins them. The 20260621010000 migration called itself a seed for 'future cross-provider identity resolution' — this is that work.

contributors.entity_id (uuid, unused) may be the intended hook. Also decide whether resolution merges rows or adds a link table; merging interacts with the UNIQUE on inat_login.
acceptance_criteria: A person observed through both providers resolves to one identity, and a native occurrence can carry an ORCID sourced from that person's iNaturalist profile.

title: Tracked .beads/issues.jsonl export is stale — auto-export isn't reaching git
description:
CORRECTED 2026-08-13: an earlier version of this issue claimed the .gitignore comment was false and that issues.jsonl was untracked. That was wrong — it IS tracked (git ls-files confirms), and the comment at .gitignore:49-58 is accurate. The real problem is narrower.

The tracked export is stale: content dates from 2026-08-04, and the last commits touching it are #368 and 9b2edde. Every bd mutation since — including this session's — exists only in the local Dolt DB and refs/dolt/data, not in the JSONL that .gitignore calls 'the recovery floor'.

Likely cause is in the comment itself: 'git hooks disabled via git config --unset core.hooksPath'. bd's auto-export writes the file but its 'git add' is refused or never runs, which is the exact silent failure the comment says happened before, when a stray rm -rf on 2026-07-27 was what surfaced it.

Fix: determine whether bd's export hook can commit under the current hooks config; if not, either re-enable the hook path or add an explicit export+commit step to the session-close protocol in CLAUDE.md. Then commit a fresh export.
acceptance_criteria: A current issues.jsonl is committed, and either the hook commits it automatically or CLAUDE.md's session-close protocol says who does.
notes:
Cause found 2026-08-29: a bare `bd export` writes to STDOUT, not to .beads/issues.jsonl. Anything piping it (`bd export | tail`, `bd export >/dev/null`) leaves the tracked file untouched while looking like it worked, and the file then drifts silently until someone diffs it. The tracked export was 14 minutes stale this session before it was noticed. The correct invocation is `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`. Whatever fix lands here, that flag is the thing a hook or alias has to carry.
FIXED 2026-08-29. Root cause: bd 1.2.2's `bd hooks run pre-commit` does no export — verified by running it directly (exit 0, no write, nothing staged) — and bd's own auto-backup last ran 2026-08-04 at 98 issues per .beads/export-state.json, against 187 today. So the mechanism the .gitignore comment assumed was never running. core.hooksPath IS set to .beads/hooks; hooks were not disabled, contrary to that comment.

Fix: an explicit export+stage step in .beads/hooks/pre-commit, placed BELOW bd's BEGIN/END markers so `bd hooks install` cannot clobber it. It warns loudly on failure and never blocks the commit. Also corrected three documents that each stated the opposite of the others: .gitignore carried a stale block saying beads is untracked directly above the block saying it is deliberately tracked; CLAUDE.md's architecture line said 'JSONL is a local-only backup, not a tracked export'; and docs/agents/issue-tracker.md said the file 'is gone'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Permalink occurrence lookup can't use an index (Sentry SALISHSEA-IO-37)
description:
hydrateFromOccurrenceId (src/salish-sea.ts:524) runs .from('occurrences').select().eq('id', 'inaturalist:340900993'). In the public.occurrences view, id is a computed string ('inaturalist:' || observations.id, and likewise per branch), so Postgres cannot push the predicate down to any index: it materializes all four UNION branches — maplify, inaturalist, happywhale, native — including the per-row photo-aggregation subqueries, then filters. Warm caches keep it under the anon role's 3s statement_timeout; a cold permalink hit blew it on 2026-08-06 (Sentry SALISHSEA-IO-37, https://beam-reach.sentry.io/issues/SALISHSEA-IO-37). Structural — will recur as permalink traffic grows.

Candidate fixes: expose an indexable source/source_id pair the client filters on (predicate pushes down per branch), or route permalink hydration through an indexed function similar to the occurrence_index path (mind decision 021's freshness constraint).
notes: Related precedent: SALISHSEA-IO-11 was the same failure shape (predicate defeating indexes under the 3s anon timeout), fixed in migration 20260803000000_occurrence_days_range_predicate.sql.
close_reason: Fixed by migration 20260812150000_occurrence_id_lookup_indexes.sql (commit 4f6e000): four expression indexes matching the pushed-down per-branch quals; verified with EXPLAIN on prod and locally with enable_seqscan=off.

title: orcasite: map machine class labels to register identifiers
description: Four-entry hardcoded map on submit_machine_detection, replacing set_attribute(:category, :whale). srkw->SSA:0000001, transient->SSA:0000002, humpback->SSA:0000901, bare OrcaHello->SSA:0000001. Safe to hardcode because ADR-0010 guarantees identifier meaning never changes — Q1 may reparent the Southern Residents but that changes membership, not identity. Machine identity belongs on detections, not item_tags: a classifier guess must not read later as a human determination. Files: server/lib/orcasite/radio/detection.ex:307
notes:
Filed upstream 2026-08-14 as orcasound/orcasite#1017.
REVISED 2026-08-14 after dthaler feedback on orcasite#1017. The four-entry single-label map was wrong: srkw and transient can both be detected in the same minute, so classification must be MULTI-VALUED. globalPredictionLabel is a seed, not the answer — OrcaHello's UI uses it only to suggest a tag and deliberately does not auto-add srkw; the real multi-class value is Metadata.tags (semicolon-delimited). Prediction already carries per-label confidence.
UPDATE 2026-08-19 from dthaler's follow-up on #1017:
(1) A FIFTH class exists in the wild: PODS-AI reports 'resident' (an oversight, per dthaler only partly deliberate). It maps to SSA:0000001 — the model was trained only on SRKW residents, not NRKW. orcahello#595 records the decision (with Dave Bain) not to add 'resident' to the hierarchy; orcahello#596 makes the moderator portal interpret resident as srkw; pods-ai#381 tracks reporting srkw directly.
(2) The 'AI: A and B' comment regex is ALREADY REPLACED upstream — PODS-AI no longer writes that format; it now pre-populates Metadata.tags with the prediction set. Nothing left to replace on that front; TagHierarchy drift point still stands.
(3) OrcaHello's DB also stores per-3-second-segment timestamps/labels/confidences within the 60s sample (which segments are srkw vs transient). orcasite lacks this; dthaler flags it as a blocker to merging the two databases. Original predictions (globalPredictionLabel + per-segment) are preserved regardless of moderation, for model improvement — the classification home in orcasite should not assume the model's assertion gets overwritten.

title: orcasite: register-aware tag picker on bouts
description: Autocomplete must read dist/searchable_name.tsv — preferred names plus common/historical/hidden alternates, so typing 'SRKW' finds the ecotype though SRKW is never offered as a name. Add the certainty affordance. Keep freeSolo: free text is never removed, so vocabulary gaps stay visible (animals README, Contributing). Form must permit zero identifications — a biophony bout may be about no animal at all. Files: ui/src/components/Bouts/BoutTags.tsx
notes:
Filed upstream 2026-08-14 as orcasound/orcasite#1015.
Register hierarchy is changing under this: salish-0gb.1 settles animals Q1 as (a), closing the ecotype vocabulary at TWO — Bigg's and Resident — with SRKW and NRKW as communities beneath Resident. orcasite#1001's premise of 'four ecotypes (SRKW, Biggs, offshore, NRKW)' will not survive it. Do not build the picker against the four-ecotype shape.
CORRECTION to the note above (2026-08-29). It said orcasite#1001's "premise of
'four ecotypes'... will not survive" the Q1 change. That was a misreading and
should not be acted on.

#1001 describes a SOLUTION — a data model giving tags `kind`, `iri` and
`certainty` — not a position on ranks and ecotypes. Its body defers to the
register explicitly ("the salish-sea/animals register supplies the identifiers
below"), and the four-ecotype phrasing Q1 quotes comes from discussion around
the proposal, not from a claim the design rests on. There is nothing there to
correct.

THE REAL DEPENDENCY, which is a data-shape one and was already anticipated by
#1001 itself: the picker renders candidates by kind and rank, from
dist/searchable_name.tsv, which #1001 notes "carries each candidate's kind and
rank". So when Q1 (a) moves Southern Resident from rank `ecotype` to rank
`community`, the picker's DISPLAY changes with it — an entity that used to
group under "ecotype" now groups under "community". Nothing about the design
changes; what it shows does. Worth knowing before the grouping is hard-coded.
SEQUENCING (decision 035, 2026-08-30): the blocked-by salish-ox2.5 dependency gates this
going LIVE -- moderators writing SSA: tags on production bouts. Building and reviewing the
picker is explicitly allowed before that ('build now, flip on after our migration', 035).
The dep is kept anyway because the register hierarchy is also changing underneath the picker
(see the salish-0gb.1 note above), so this should not surface in bd ready as buildable yet.
If the migration stalls and picker work becomes urgent, split an activation issue out and
move the dependency there rather than deleting it.
GRAPH FIX 2026-08-30 (CodeRabbit on salishsea-io#417): the blocked-by salish-ox2.5 edge added
earlier today gated this whole issue, but decision 035 gates only going live. The gate moved to
salish-8vr.24 (activation), blocked by both ox2.5 and this issue. This one is buildable whenever
its own prerequisites are -- see the salish-0gb.1 note above about the ecotype shape.

title: Migrate from npm to pnpm
description:
npm's lockfile is host-specific for optional platform deps: running `npm install` on darwin prunes packages reachable only through optional wasm32-wasi/platform bindings, then linux CI computes an ideal tree that wants them and `npm ci` fails EUSAGE. This has now broken main twice (8cc5572/41924ba, fixed in bc86cb2) and previously via the @rolldown/@emnapi pruning noted in engineering lessons. Upstream: npm/cli#4828, open since 2022.

pnpm records every platform variant unconditionally, so the failure mode cannot occur. Migrate the root project and infra/, update all five workflows, and switch the Dependabot npm ecosystem over.
design:
pnpm over Yarn Berry (PnP fights Vite tooling; node-modules linker forfeits the benefit) and over Bun (adds a second, less battle-tested runtime to CI, cutting against the project's 'minimize volatile dependencies' constraint).

Scope:
- pnpm import to convert package-lock.json -> pnpm-lock.yaml (root and infra/)
- packageManager field in package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml if infra/ becomes a workspace
- .github/workflows: build.yml, deploy.yml, smoke.yml, dwca-nightly.yml, ingest-heartbeat.yml -- pnpm/action-setup + 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile', cache: pnpm in setup-node
- .github/dependabot.yml: npm ecosystem reads pnpm-lock.yaml (supported for lockfileVersion 9)
- docs: README.md, infra/README.md, CLAUDE.md build/test block, docs/runbook/deploys.md, docs/engineering-lessons.md
- decision record in docs/decisions/
acceptance_criteria: All five workflows green on main; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds in a clean clone on linux; package-lock.json deleted; decision record written; docs reference pnpm commands.
close_reason: Merged as PR #370 (a4fb368) and deployed to production successfully on 2026-08-04. First pnpm deploy green end to end: Build, Test, Deploy (supabase db push + S3/CloudFront + pnpm exec cdk deploy), Smoke. Decision record docs/decisions/025-pnpm-over-npm.md. Also brought infra/ under Dependabot, which had never been covered.

title: No CI guard against SELECT-grant drift between migrations and prod
description:
salish-0ew shipped migration 20260730120000_public_select_grants.sql, which brought a fresh `supabase db reset` to grant parity with prod (48 = 48). Nothing stops it drifting again.

The gap that caused salish-0ew was invisible precisely because prod looked correct: grants were applied out of band, and every later `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` preserved them, so nothing ever disturbed prod and nothing ever recreated them elsewhere. The same thing can happen again the next time a grant is applied by hand.

The only guard today is the grant-replay step in scripts/pull-prod-db.sh, which runs locally when someone mirrors prod. It makes the mirror work; it does not fail anything.

Opportunity: as of PR #368 build.yml is also the deploy gate, so an assertion added there blocks production, not just PRs. It already runs `supabase db start` and applies supabase/ci-seed.sql, so the reset database is in hand.
acceptance_criteria: A CI check fails when the grants produced by a fresh reset differ from an expected set — either a checked-in expected-grants fixture diffed in build.yml, or an assertion hitting the anon REST path against the freshly reset CI database. Lives in build.yml so it gates deploys as well as PRs.
notes: This is acceptance criterion 3 of salish-0ew, which was closed with criteria 1 and 2 met. Reproduce the original diff per that issue: information_schema.role_table_grants for table_schema in ('public','dwc'), grantee in ('anon','authenticated'), privilege_type='SELECT'. Run psql with timing OFF or the '\timing' line inflates the count by one.

description:
Replacing the date input with a calendar (salish-dq2, decision 021) removed the only way to jump to a distant date. The corpus spans 2012-2026, so reaching the earliest data now takes 169 clicks on the month arrow.

Make the 'Thu, Jul 30, 2026' readout under the grid click-to-edit: it swaps in a native <input type=date> bounded by the same range the calendar enforces, commits on change, and reverts on Escape or blur.
design:
Option B of the options discussed 2026-07-31. Chosen over year steppers (still 14 clicks to 2012, no information) and over a drill-up month/year picker (option A — more capable, since it would also show WHICH months have data, but a bigger build). B does not foreclose A; the drill-up can host a typed-date field later.

Bounds come from EARLIEST_OBSERVATION_DATE and observationToday() so the input and the grid cannot disagree.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking the date readout swaps in a focused date input; entering a date selects it and reverts to the readout; Escape and blur revert without changing the date; the input cannot select outside 2000-01-01..today.

title: Revoke inert anon/authenticated write grants on public relations
description:
Production grants `anon` and `authenticated` INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on 44 `public` relations. Nothing needs them and no migration created them.

Found 2026-07-30 alongside salish-0ew; deliberately left out of that fix so a parity migration did not also change production's permissions.

## Not a vulnerability

Checked every RLS policy in `public` on 2026-07-30:

- Every table carrying these grants has RLS **enabled**.
- **No policy permits an anon write.** Every anon policy is `FOR SELECT`. The `FOR ALL` policies on `observations` and `observation_photos` are scoped to `authenticated` with ownership predicates (`user_uuid = auth.uid()`, or a contributor-join).
- The remaining relations are views (`occurrences`, `occurrence_days`, `individual_occurrences`, `group_occurrences`, `ecotype_occurrences`, `occurrence_identifications`, `occurrence_unresolved_codes`). They are UNION/aggregate views, so they are not auto-updatable and a write fails regardless of grant.

So the grants are inert. This is cleanup, not an incident.

## Why bother

They are a loaded footgun. The moment someone adds a permissive policy to one of these tables -- entirely reasonable in isolation -- the write grant is already sitting there and the table becomes anon-writable. Defence in depth wants the grant absent, so that a policy mistake alone is not sufficient.

Also included: `GRANT SELECT ON public.contributor_email_addresses TO anon, authenticated`, reproduced in migration `20260730120000` purely to match prod. It is inert today (RLS on, zero policies, default deny) but should not exist.

## The care this needs

`authenticated` genuinely writes to `observations` and `observation_photos` -- the sighting form's path. Revoking too broadly breaks contribution, and the failure would be silent for anonymous readers and loud only for logged-in contributors, so it will not show up in a smoke test that does not log in.

Work out exactly which grants the write paths depend on before revoking anything. `sighting-form.ts` goes through `rpc('upsert_observation')`, which may be SECURITY DEFINER and therefore not need direct table grants at all -- confirm rather than assume, and check the delete and photo-attachment paths too.

Revoke in a migration (so local/CI/prod stay reconciled), not out of band -- out-of-band changes are exactly what caused salish-0ew.
acceptance_criteria:
- The write paths (`upsert_observation`, delete, photo attachment) are traced and documented, establishing which grants `authenticated` actually requires.
- A migration revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from `anon` on all 44 relations, and from `authenticated` on everything the traced paths do not need.
- `SELECT` on `public.contributor_email_addresses` is revoked from `anon` and `authenticated` in the same migration.
- A logged-in contributor can still create, edit and delete a sighting with photos, verified against a database built from migrations.
- Anonymous read of the map, list and calendar is unaffected.
notes:
Write-path analysis done 2026-07-31; implementation not started.

FINDING: public.upsert_observation is SECURITY INVOKER, not DEFINER (prosecdef=false, owner=postgres). It therefore runs with the caller's privileges, so 'authenticated' genuinely needs direct table grants — the guess in this issue's description that it might be DEFINER, and so need none, was wrong.

It writes exactly two tables: public.observations and public.observation_photos. Separately, src/obs-summary.ts:316 does a direct .from('observations').delete().

So the minimum 'authenticated' actually needs is:
  INSERT, UPDATE on public.observations
  INSERT, UPDATE on public.observation_photos
  DELETE on public.observations
and 'anon' needs none of the 44 write grants at all.

BLOCKED ON A DECISION (do not start without it):
  (a) Narrow revoke — strip anon entirely, trim authenticated to the five grants above. Low risk, keeps the current security model.
  (b) Make upsert_observation SECURITY DEFINER — then authenticated needs no direct write grants and every write goes through one audited function. Stronger, but it changes the write path's security model and wants its own decision record.

Reverted to open 2026-07-31 rather than left in_progress: the analysis is recorded, but nothing should be implemented until (a) or (b) is chosen.

title: Regions filter the data, and shade the map outside the active region
description:
Follow-on to #352 (Go-to place bubbles) and encompassing GH issue #16 ("Shade map area outside the bounds of the data").

## Why

Today the region bubbles are pure navigation: clicking one zooms the map and nothing else changes. Two problems follow.

1. Absence reads as absence. A user who pans past the edge of our ingest coverage sees empty water and concludes there were no whales there, when in fact we carry no data there at all. That is GH #16.
2. The region is not a durable piece of state. Pan away and the framing is gone; there is nothing to share, nothing in the URL, and no way to say "show me Puget Sound" as a question about the data rather than about the viewport.

Promoting regions from viewport presets to a filter fixes both: the region becomes the scope of the query, and the area outside it is shaded to say plainly "we are not showing you anything here."

## What

A selected region filters the occurrence data and masks the map outside itself. It persists across pan and zoom, survives reload, and is shareable.

Salish Sea is the default.
design:
Decided with the user 2026-07-30:

**1. The mask means "the region you selected", not "where our coverage ends."**
One concept, one mask. Picking a region both filters the data and shades everything outside it. Rejected: a separate permanent coverage mask derived from source/taxon extents layered under a lighter region outline (truer to #16's framing, but two overlapping shaded areas to design and caption); and shading the intersection of region and coverage (single mask whose meaning shifts depending on which constraint binds).

**2. Regions stay lon/lat rectangles.**
Reuse the existing `Extent` constants in src/constants.ts. The filter is exact and predictable and this ships without sourcing new geodata. Accepted cost: a rectangle shaded over the Salish Sea is crude -- it clips Puget Sound's south end and includes Vancouver Island's interior. Rejected for now: real polygons (Salish Sea water body, NOAA SRKW critical habitat) -- better-looking and semantically real, but needs sourcing, licensing, simplification and a home (static GeoJSON vs a PostGIS table). Also rejected: bbox filter + polygon mask, which makes the shading and the filter disagree at the edges (points visible inside a shaded corner).

**3. The filter applies to the map, the observation list, AND the calendar's day counts.**
Everything the sidebar shows must agree. If the calendar counted sightings the map is not drawing, a day would read "busy" and click through to empty water -- the exact confusion this issue exists to remove. See the RESOLVED section in the notes: only the calendar needs a schema change; the map and list filter through plain PostgREST.

**4. Every bubble filters.** Puget Sound, Salish Sea, San Juans, SRKW Range -- one control, one meaning. Picking San Juans hides a sighting off Victoria 20 miles away; acceptable because the mask makes the hiding visible. Rejected: coarse regions filter while fine ones only navigate (two visually identical bubbles doing different things).

**5. "Salish Sea" as a filter means `salishSeaExtent` = [-126, 47, -122, 50.5]** -- NOT the `salishSRKWExtent` = [-124, 47, -122, 49.5] the bubble uses today. Settled 2026-07-30, resolving open item (a). The tight SRKW-clipped extent was chosen in #352 to frame "the water the sightings are actually in", which is right for a viewport and wrong for a filter: as the default it would silently drop the Strait of Georgia north of 49.5 and the whole western Strait of Juan de Fuca / Swiftsure Bank west of -124. Implementation note: decide explicitly whether the *zoom* keeps the tight extent while the *filter* uses the wide one, or both widen. Two extents for one bubble needs a comment saying why, or it reads as a bug.

**6. There is an "Everywhere" escape hatch.** Settled 2026-07-30, resolving open item (b). Without it the widest region is SRKW Range [-125.5, 36, -122, 54] while ingest reaches `acartiaExtent` [-136, 36, -120, 54], leaving real data permanently unreachable from the UI. "Everywhere" drops the region filter entirely (and draws no mask). Costs one more bubble in an already-full row -- worth watching at 390px width, where the Go-to row is already the tightest thing in the panel.

**Assumed, not asked:** selecting a region still zooms the map to it, as the bubbles do today. The filter is what is new; the navigation is retained.
acceptance_criteria:
- Selecting a region filters the map features, the sidebar observation list, and the calendar's per-day volume circles, consistently.
- The filter persists across pan, zoom, day changes, reload and back/forward; it is encoded in the URL and a shared link reproduces it.
- The map area outside the active region is visibly shaded, in a treatment that reads as "we are not showing data here", satisfying GH #16.
- Salish Sea is the default on a fresh load with no region in the URL, using `salishSeaExtent` per design decision 5.
- The `occurrence_days` change is verified against prod-scale data: the month predicate still pushes down through the GROUP BY into each UNION branch with the bbox added, and a month still returns within the latency budget decision 021 set (~120-170 ms). NOT an index requirement — prod has no spatial index and this issue explicitly does not add one; see the measurements in the notes.
- Decision record written; docs/decisions/README.md updated; GH #16 closed by the PR.
notes:
Open items to settle during implementation, in rough priority order:

**a. The "Salish Sea" extent is wrong for a filter.** The bubble uses `salishSRKWExtent` = [-124, 47, -122, 49.5], deliberately, because #352 wanted framing on "the water the sightings are actually in". As the DEFAULT FILTER it silently drops real data: everything in the Strait of Georgia north of 49.5, and the whole western Strait of Juan de Fuca / Swiftsure Bank west of -124. `salishSeaExtent` = [-126, 47, -122, 50.5] is the honest choice for filtering. Consider keeping the tight extent for the zoom and the wide one for the filter, or just widening both. Resolve before implementing -- it decides what the default hides.

**b. No escape hatch was chosen.** The widest bubble is SRKW Range [-125.5, 36, -122, 54]; ingest reaches `acartiaExtent` [-136, 36, -120, 54]. With every bubble a filter and no "Everywhere" option, data in that gap becomes unreachable from the UI. Either add an "Everywhere" bubble, or accept and document that the app only ever shows the SRKW range at widest.

**c. URL state.** The region needs a param (`?r=puget-sound` or similar) alongside `d`/`x`/`y`/`z`/`o`, with slugs, validation and a popstate path. See `parseUrlParams`/`setQueryParams` in src/salish-sea.ts.

**d. `?o=` pointing outside the active region.** `hydrateFromOccurrenceId` can land on an occurrence the current filter excludes. Widen the region to fit it, or clear the filter, or refuse -- needs a decision.

**e. Realtime and the sighting form.** The `occurrences_changed` broadcast refetch must carry the region. A contributor can save a sighting outside the active region (the form validates against `acartiaExtent`) and then not see it -- decide whether saving widens or clears the filter.

**f. Mask rendering.** An OpenLayers layer drawing world-minus-region. Needs a treatment that reads as "no data here" rather than "disabled", and must not swallow map interactions or the basemap's own legibility.

**g. Out of scope:** individual/matriline profile page maps, and the DwC-A export.

**h. Write a decision record** for the mask-means-selected-region and rectangles-for-now calls before implementing -- per CLAUDE.md, decisions get written when made.

---

## Measured on prod, 2026-07-30 (corpus: 61,389 occurrences; 39,608 maplify + 20,569 iNat)

Bbox filtering is cheap, but NOT because of an index -- there is no spatial index and, as the view is written, there cannot be one.

| query | time |
|---|---|
| A. `occurrence_days`, one month, no region (today's calendar) | **169 ms** |
| B. same month + Salish Sea bbox | **75 ms** |
| C. Salish Sea bbox with NO day filter (whole corpus) | **3,448 ms** |
| D. bbox on `maplify.sightings` base table (`&&` envelope) | 20 ms (seq scan, 39.6k rows) |
| E. bbox on `inaturalist.observations` base table | 11 ms (seq scan, 20.6k rows) |

**Adding the region makes the calendar query faster, not slower** (169 -> 75 ms). The bbox cuts rows before they reach the view's nested-loop joins against taxa/providers/collections/organizations, which are seq-scanned per row -- the maplify branch alone reports 5.8M "Rows Removed by Join Filter". Those joins, not the spatial predicate, are what the month query actually spends its time on.

**There is no spatial index in prod.** 74 indexes across public/maplify/inaturalist/happywhale; zero GiST, zero on any `location` column.

**An index would not help anyway, for two independent reasons:**
1. `public.occurrences.location` is not a geography -- it is a computed composite, `row(gis.ST_X(location::gis.geometry), gis.ST_Y(location::gis.geometry))::lon_lat`. Any predicate against the view's `location` is an expression over the base column and can never use an index on it. Using one would mean pushing the predicate into the base tables, inside the view or inside a function.
2. The Salish Sea bbox matches **38,272 of 61,389 rows (62%)**. At that selectivity the planner would choose a seq scan over a GiST index regardless.

**Do not add a spatial index as part of this work.** It would be dead weight at this corpus size. Revisit if the corpus grows an order of magnitude or if regions become polygons (design item 2), where `ST_Intersects` against a real shape is a genuinely more expensive predicate.

**Row C is the trap to avoid:** any region query that omits a date bound costs ~3.5 s. Every code path that filters by region must also bound the day.

---

## RESOLVED 2026-07-30: PostgREST can filter the composite. No RPC needed for map or list.

Tested against a full production mirror in the local stack (`scripts/pull-prod-db.sh`). The earlier worry that `location` being a composite rather than jsonb would force everything through RPC functions was **wrong**.

**`->` works and is exact.** A four-sided bbox via the REST API returned `Content-Range: 0-0/38275`, matching `SELECT count(*)` in SQL for the same bbox exactly (38,275):

```
/rest/v1/occurrences?select=id
  &location->lon=gte.-126&location->lon=lte.-122
  &location->lat=gte.47&location->lat=lte.50.5
```

In supabase-js: `.gte('location->lon', -126).lte('location->lon', -122)` and likewise for `lat`.

**`->>` is a silent trap. Do not use it.** The same query with `->>` returned `Content-Range: */0` -- zero rows, no error. `->>` yields text, so the bounds compare lexically instead of numerically and quietly match nothing. Worth a comment at the call site.

**Consequence for scope:** the map query and the observation list need NO migration -- plain PostgREST filters on `from('occurrences')`. Only the calendar needs a schema change, because `occurrence_days` aggregates and the bbox must apply before the `GROUP BY`; the view exposes only `day` and `occurrence_count`, so there is nothing for a client-side predicate to bite on. That is a function taking bbox arguments, and it is the ONLY database work this issue requires. Design item 3 stands as written.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #357 (merged 2026-07-31). Regions filter the map, observation list and calendar day counts; ?r= in the URL; map outside the active region is shaded. Closes GH #16. Decision record: docs/decisions/022-regions-filter-data.md.

title: CI runs two different Supabase CLI versions
description:
build.yml starts the database with the CLI that supabase/setup-cli puts on PATH (pinned 2.53.6), but 'npm run gen-types' resolves node_modules/.bin/supabase first — the devDependency (2.107.0). So the DB is started by one CLI and its types generated by another, and neither is obviously the intended one.

This is what made salish-cr0's sibling bug hard to see: setup-cli exports SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY=ghcr.io and 2.53.6 honours it for 'db start', while 2.107.0 ignored it for 'gen types' (supabase/cli#5785) and pulled postgres-meta from public.ecr.aws, hitting the 1 pull/sec anonymous limit.

deploy.yml also uses setup-cli 2.53.6 for 'supabase link', 'functions deploy' and 'db push' against production, so any unification has to weigh bumping the CLI that runs prod migrations.
design: Options: (a) drop setup-cli from build.yml and use npx supabase everywhere, setting SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY=ghcr.io explicitly since that env var is currently a setup-cli side effect; (b) bump setup-cli's pin to match the devDependency. (a) gives one version and makes the registry choice explicit; (b) is smaller but leaves two sources of truth.
acceptance_criteria: A single Supabase CLI version is used across build.yml, and the version is traceable to one place.
notes: PR #382 open: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/pull/382 — devDep ^2.114.0, build.yml uses it via pnpm exec (registry env now explicit at job level), deploy.yml's setup-cli resolves the version from pnpm-lock.yaml. Close on merge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #382 (ceafe7e): build.yml uses the supabase devDependency via pnpm exec, deploy.yml's setup-cli resolves the version from pnpm-lock.yaml — one CLI (2.114.0), one source of truth.

title: Inner joins in the DwC export can silently drop occurrence records
description:
dwc._native_occurrences inner-joins public.contributors on contributor_id (20260621000000_dwc_view_rebuild.sql:98), but contributor_id was relaxed from NOT NULL to nullable (20260619203013_source_table_fk_columns.sql:44). title: The taxa refresh cannot record a replacement it does not already mirror
description:
Seven of the nine retired taxa in the mirror carry current_taxon_id = NULL even though
iNaturalist named a successor for each: 508823->508822, 520333->1651787, 531609->1661364,
1289590->1246814, 1368489->1672273, 1368490->1672272, 1368492->1664972. The refresh
reports each one every run ("replacement N is not mirrored; recorded as retired only").

WHY IT HAPPENS

inaturalist.taxa.current_taxon_id is a foreign key, and the mirror holds only taxa the
ingest closure has fetched. scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts therefore cannot record a
pointer to a taxon it does not hold, and it does not fetch one: pulling in a successor
drags in that successor's whole ancestor chain, which is the closure's job.

The ingest DOES follow current_taxon_id since salish-5ds, but only for a taxon entering
the mirror. These seven are already held, so nothing re-asks and nothing ever fetches
their successors.

WHY IT MATTERS LITTLE TODAY

Nothing references any of the seven (checked in prod 2026-08-29), and under decision 032 a
retirement with no replacement displays under its own name, which is the honest answer.
The cost shows up only if a record lands on one of them, and iNaturalist reassigns
observations to the successor when it retires a taxon, so that is unlikely.

OPTIONS IF IT IS EVER WORTH FIXING

- Let the refresh fetch a missing successor and insert it with its ancestor chain, which
  means giving the script a closure resolver (or importing resolveTaxonClosure).
- Have the refresh record the successor id in a nullable column with no FK, and resolve
  through it only when the target happens to be mirrored. Cheaper, but it splits "the
  replacement" across two columns.
- Leave it. The state is honest and reported on every run.

Related: decision 032, salish-5ds, migration 20260828000000.

title: Sentry init is PROD-gated on one entry point and not the other three
description:
`src/salish-sea.ts:31` guards `sentryClient.init()` with `import.meta.env.PROD`; `individual-page.ts:16`, `matriline-page.ts:15` and `ecotype-page.ts:15` call it unconditionally. So dev sessions on the profile pages already report to the production DSN, tagged `environment: development`.

Separately, `getCurrentScope().setClient(sentryClient)` in `src/sentry.ts` runs at import on every entry point, and the BrowserClient constructor builds its transport whenever a DSN is present. `init()` only installs integrations — so a direct `captureException` (as `receiveIdToken` now does, decision 030) transmits in dev regardless of the PROD guard.

Decide whether dev events are wanted at all, then make all four entry points agree. Either gate `setClient` on PROD, or drop the guard in salish-sea.ts and rely on the `environment` tag for filtering.

Found by adversarial review of PR #403.
notes: PR #422: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/pull/422 — gated Sentry to PROD at the binding, not init(). The gate/don't-gate choice is flagged in the PR for the owner; flipping it is one line. Awaiting merge.
close_reason: Merged in #422. One initSentry() in sentry.ts that all four entry points call; gates the scope binding, not init(), since binding is what makes captureException transmit. sentryClient unexported. Chose not to send dev events (alternative was filtering on the environment tag) — stated as an assumption in the PR; reversing it is one line, and a decision record should follow if confirmed.

title: Symbology at historical density (029 open question, GH #31)
description:
Left open by decision 029. Everything measured for it covers 33-106 occurrences
in a day. The busiest day on record is 185, and the historical view (GH #31)
would exceed that by orders of magnitude.

Untested at that scale: whether layer-level declutter keeps up, whether the
labels degrade usefully (they drop rather than shrink), and whether 60+ segments
of travel line read as anything but a mesh.

The prototype's variant C ("Density" — no labels, radius by count, opacity by
age) exists on branch prototype/map-symbology and was built for exactly this
question. It is the obvious starting point rather than a fresh design.

title: What makes a track worth drawing? (029 open question)
description:
Left open by decision 029 and unchanged by its implementation.

A 2-point, sub-hour segment is a thin claim to render as a journey — the map
draws a line and an arrow, which asserts the animal travelled that way, from two
sightings that may be two people seeing the same whale from opposite shores. The
threshold probably wants 3+ points or a minimum distance.

Now more visible than when 029 was written, because the head label says
"Seen 2× in under an hour" out loud — the map is stating the weakness of its own
claim in words.

Relevant: imputeSegmentFrom already gates on 12h, 20km, and 3x the taxon's mean
travel speed (src/segments.ts). This is about what to DRAW, not what to chain.

title: Pooled matriline identifiers make the label too long for a phone
description:
Visible on production 2026-08-27, the first real day under decision 029:

  Biggs · T137A, T36, T36Bs, T137, T137Bs
  Seen 5× over 3h

The identity line pools identifiers across the whole segment (salish-ayb.6 /
#402), which is right — a matriline named in one sighting of an encounter and
not the next still names the track. But a 5-point Biggs encounter can name four
or five matrilines, and the line reaches ~45 characters. On a phone that is most
of the screen width, and it is the one label a reader most wants.

029 did not anticipate it: its worked example is "Gray whale · CRC53", one
identifier. The record's own worry was name length, and the register fixed that;
this is the same problem arriving from the other side.

Options, none decided:
  * Cap the list and count the rest — "T137A, T36 +3".
  * Drop to the matriline root — T137A/T137Bs/T137 are all T137s.
  * Let the second line carry them, since it already exists for multi-point
    tracks and is where "what happened" lives.

Do not simply un-pool them: the head would then name whichever matrilines the
LAST sighting happened to mention, which is worse and arbitrary.

title: maskLayer's zIndex works only because OpenLayers' sort sees NaN
description:
obs-map.ts gives maskLayer zIndex: 1 with a comment saying it belongs "above
the basemap, below the occurrences". Every other layer in the stack leaves
zIndex undefined.

OpenLayers sorts layer states with (a, b) => a.zIndex - b.zIndex
(ol/renderer/Composite.js). ol/layer/Base.js sets state.zIndex to the layer's
zIndex, which is `undefined` for a managed layer that was never given one. So
every comparison between the mask (1) and anything else is `1 - undefined` =
NaN, V8 treats a NaN comparator result as "equal", and the sort is a no-op.
Paint order is array order, which happens to be what the comment describes.

Taken literally, zIndex: 1 would put the mask ABOVE the occurrences and shade
the sightings it exists to distinguish from empty water — the opposite of GH
#16's intent.

Nothing is visibly wrong today. The hazard is that the next person to set an
explicit zIndex on any other layer turns the comparisons real and silently
reorders the map. Fix is to drop zIndex: 1 and rely on array order (the stack
is already ordered correctly), or give every layer an explicit zIndex.

Found while reordering the infrastructure layers for salish-fll.3.

title: Correct a false claim in migration 20260828110000: dwc DOES read public.occurrences
description:
The header of supabase/migrations/20260828110000_occurrences_register_names.sql says:

  "The DwC-A export emits no vernacularName and nothing in `dwc` reads this view, so the
   archive is unaffected."

The second clause is false. Four of the six dwc relations read public.occurrences:
_maplify_occurrences, _native_occurrences, datasets, occurrences.

The conclusion still holds — no dwc relation has a vernacular column, so the register
display-name change genuinely did not touch the archive — but the stated reason is wrong,
and it is the kind of claim someone will rely on. It nearly misled me an hour later while
sizing salish-a4y, where "does dwc read this view" is the difference between a display
tweak and a change to what we publish.

Found because I checked pg_get_viewdef on the dwc relations directly rather than trusting
a pg_depend query that had already missed two dependents earlier the same day.

Fix the comment in place; no behaviour change.

title: Restate DwC-A coverage once ingest scope is filtered
description:
The dwc schema reads public.occurrences (4 of its 6 relations), so filtering scope there
changes the published archive — roughly 17,620 Maplify records leave it.

That is defensible and arguably overdue: an archive under a Salish Sea remit should not be
publishing Californian humpbacks. But decision 027 and rights-policy §6.5 state coverage
deliberately, and verify-artifact's SC#4c gates the build on that prose, so the change has
to be reflected rather than discovered.

Check whether geographicCoverage in eml.xml states a bounding box, and whether it matches
the new scope. Re-run the GBIF validator afterwards.
notes:
Downgraded: no consumers of the export today, so this is follow-up rather than a gate on
the filter shipping.
close_reason: EML geographicDescription and rights-policy §6.5 restated in PR #419; bbox unchanged (orcas range-wide). GBIF validator NOT re-run — no consumers; rerun when someone consumes the export

title: Nothing re-asks iNaturalist about taxa we already hold
description:
Surfaced by salish-ayb.4, and broader than the deactivation problem it was filed under.

`resolveTaxonClosure` (supabase/functions/ingest/fetch-inaturalist.ts) diffs referenced
taxa against what we store and fetches only the MISSING ones. So a taxon row is written
once, at first sighting, and upstream is never asked about it again. `ON CONFLICT DO
NOTHING` in persist.ts is not the cause and changing it fixes nothing — the row is never
re-offered.

Consequences beyond deactivation:

  - vernacular_name never updates. iNaturalist renames common names; ours are frozen at
    whatever they were when the taxon first appeared. This matters directly for
    salish-ayb.5: the display name we are about to stop using comes from this column.
  - rank and parent_id likewise.
  - is_active and current_taxon_id (added 2026-08-28) can only be maintained by the
    v1-based refresh script, since the ingest's v2 endpoint omits inactive taxa entirely.

scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts refreshes deactivation status on demand. What is
missing is (a) something that runs it, and (b) extending it to the other mirror fields.

Options for (a): a scheduled GitHub Action like the animals crosswalk check, a pg_cron
job, or folding it into the nightly DwC-A build. A weekly cadence is plenty — nine
retirements accumulated over the mirror's whole lifetime.

Whatever runs it must not clobber is_active/current_taxon_id from a v2 response, which
cannot see them.
notes:
ALSO IN SCOPE (from the adversarial review of #396): the nightly ingest can revert a
repoint of inaturalist.observations.taxon_id. persist.ts upserts
'taxon_id = EXCLUDED.taxon_id WHERE EXCLUDED.updated_at > ...', so if upstream still
reports the retired id on a record whose updated_at advances (a comment, a fave, an edit),
the mirror flips back. The FK still passes, because the retired taxon remains mirrored.

Deeper point worth a decision rather than a quiet fix: that column is UPSTREAM's, unlike
maplify.sightings.taxon_id which we derive ourselves. Rewriting it is in tension with
decision 008's rule that source schemas are verbatim mirrors. The honest options are to
resolve retirements at read time in the occurrences view, to have the ingest itself follow
current_taxon_id when it writes, or to accept the mirror carrying a dead id and translate
downstream. Currently we do the third badly: a batch repair that upstream can undo.
close_reason:
Closed by #408 (read-time resolution, decision 032) and #409 (weekly refresh), both deployed 2026-08-29.

(a) Nothing re-asked about taxa we hold: .github/workflows/taxa-refresh.yml now runs scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts --apply Mondays 03:00 PT via the DwC-A nightly's session-pooler DSN (no new secret), files a taxa-refresh-failed issue, and puts the diff in the job summary. The script refreshes every mirrored field, not just status, and asks through the ingest's own taxaUrl/parseInatTaxa so the two cannot drift. First run (33267002050) fixed 13 stale prod rows: 8 vernacular names (41472 Inia geoffrensis read 'Boto', now 'Amazon River Dolphin') and 5 genera whose parent moved when iNaturalist inserted the seal tribes. DwC family/genus unchanged, 28345/28345 still populated.

(b) The taxon_id question, settled as decision 032: resolve on read, never rewrite. A stored id records what was claimed (upstream's, or a contributor's determination); public.occurrences and dwc.taxa_classification hop through current_taxon_id, hopping at every ancestor step in the classification because parent_id is the one link a repointing script refuses to touch. All repointing removed, so the revert risk in this issue's notes is gone by construction.

INCIDENT, worth knowing: teaching inaturalist.species_id() to resolve a retired parent turned a pure CASE into a function with a table read. A view checks referenced objects against its OWNER; a function BODY is checked against the CALLER, and anon lacks USAGE on the inaturalist schema, so every anonymous read of public.occurrences 42501'd. Smoke caught it, fixed in ~6 min with SECURITY DEFINER + empty search_path (migration 20260829040000). Testing via psql as postgres cannot see this; 'SET ROLE anon' reproduces it, and a test now does.

title: Travel lines: absent at default zoom, faint when present (GH #271)
description:
GH #271 reports travel lines as barely visible. Two separate causes found
during the symbology prototype:

1. ABSENT, not faint. `travelStyle` returns early when `resolution > 100`. At
   48N, zoom 10 is ~102 m/px and the app's default view is wider than that, so
   travel lines do not draw at all until the user zooms in past ~zoom 11. A
   user reporting "you can hardly see them" may be looking at a map where they
   are not rendered.
2. FAINT when they do draw. 2 px of #ffcc33 with no casing disappears into the
   Esri basemap's coastline. The prototype added a white casing stroke beneath
   the line, which is what actually makes it read.

Both belong in the symbology decision rather than being patched separately,
since how loud the line should be is inseparable from whether the segment is
the primary labelled object.

Public issue: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/issues/271
close_reason: PR #401. Measured the default Salish Sea view at 489 m/px against the old resolution>100 gate — the lines were absent, not faint. Gate removed from the line, kept for the annotations (arrows, imputed present position). White casing under the 2px #ffcc33. Verified headless at res 489 and at zoom 13.

title: Occurrence markers and infrastructure markers read as the same visual class
description:
Hydrophones, viewing locations and salmon counting sites draw as circular
badges at roughly the same size as occurrence bubbles, so on the live map a
hydrophone reads as a sighting. Visible in any screenshot of the current map:
the circle-with-waves icons sit in the same visual register as the lettered
occurrence circles.

Whatever symbology lands, occurrences and infrastructure need to be
distinguishable classes — different shape, different weight, or different
saturation — not merely different glyphs inside the same circle.

Surfaced during the symbology prototype, 2026-08-27.
close_reason: PR #401. All three infrastructure icons move to a rounded-square plate and the viewing-location eye off #3399CC (the occurrence blue) onto the shared #1e2b76. Infrastructure layers moved below travel and occurrences. Shape was chosen over colour deliberately: it survives whatever palette 029's taxon colours land on. Filed salish-qfg for the maskLayer zIndex hazard found while reordering.

title: North Pacific Humpback never seeds a travel segment (missing travelSpeedKmH entry)
description:
`src/segments.ts` looks up `travelSpeedKmH[start.taxon.scientific_name]` by
exact match. `src/constants.ts` has six entries and
`Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira` is not one of them, so 319 occurrences of North
Pacific Humpback Whale can never START a segment, while plain
`Megaptera novaeangliae` (17,933 records) can.

Decision 027 records that the empty entries in that table are intent, not
oversight — pinnipeds and otters are excluded deliberately. This is different:
the subspecies of an included species is excluded by accident of exact-string
matching.

Check the same class of bug for other subspecies present in the corpus:
Orcinus orca ater and rectipinnus ARE listed; Phocoena phocoena vomerina and
Phoca vitulina richardii are not, though those taxa are excluded on purpose
anyway.

Fix is either a table entry or matching on species_id, which segments.ts
already uses for the candidate comparison one line later.
close_reason: PR #401. travelSpeedFor() falls back trinomial -> binomial; reaches Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira (342 prod records) and Balaenoptera acutorostrata scammoni (2), leaves 027's deliberate omissions omitted at every rank, and lets an explicit subspecies key still win. Prod confirmed species_id is shared across subspecies (41566 humpbacks, 41521 orcas), so only the seed lookup was failing.

title: Emit coordinateUncertaintyInMeters: what the accuracy audit means for the export
description:
Context for salish-6dy, from the symbology accuracy audit (2026-08-27).

`accuracy` on public.occurrences is NULL for maplify (34,791) and direct (438),
carries three discrete coordinate-precision values for happywhale (2/16/161 m),
and for iNaturalist ranges p50 31 m to a max of 7,313 km across 16,410 of
20,581 records.

Two consequences for the DwC-A:
  - SRC-01 excludes iNaturalist and HappyWhale, which are the only providers
    with any value at all. So the exported archive would emit
    coordinateUncertaintyInMeters on approximately zero records. Worth
    confirming before building the field.
  - Where a value does exist it describes reporter position, not animal
    position, which is not what coordinateUncertaintyInMeters means for an
    occurrence record. Emitting it unqualified would overstate precision to
    GBIF consumers.

Relates to salish-6dy. Filed separately so the audit is not lost in it.

title: Short-form map labels: our presentation layer over the register's names
description:
ADR-0011 is explicit that this is ours: `label` is "input to display, not
display", and the register "cannot know whether a consumer needs a dropdown
entry, a map pin, a sentence fragment, a chart axis, or twenty characters on a
phone". Truncation and capitalisation are named as consumer concerns.

So a map pin saying "Humpback" rather than "Humpback whale" is legitimate, and
is a DIFFERENT change from adopting "River otter" over "North American River
Otter" — the latter is fixing a wrong name (the register's job), the former is
composing a short form (ours).

It is not a general rule. "Humpback whale" -> "Humpback" works because the
modifier is a noun; "Gray whale" -> "Gray" does not. So it is a curated short
form per taxon, keyed by SSA identifier, living in this repo as presentation
config — not as another name row, and never by writing back into the register.

Longest names currently reaching the map, for sizing the work:
  Eastern Pacific Long-beaked Common Dolphin  42 chars
  North Pacific Humpback Whale                28
  Pacific White-sided Dolphin                 27
  North American River Otter                  26
  Resident Killer Whale                       21   (4,115 records)

Blocked on the materialization issue: there is no SSA identifier to key on
until occurrences resolve to register entities.
close_reason:
PR #402. Short forms keyed on the register's SSA identifier, carried onto taxon by migration 20260829000000; shipped with decision 029's implementation because the map had nowhere to render a short form until it existed.

Only FIVE entries were needed — Humpback, White-sided dolphin, Elephant seal, Bottlenose dolphin, Right whale dolphin. The issue sized this against iNaturalist's names (42, 28, 27, 26 chars); adopting the register in ayb.5 already fixed those, and most register names are the right length for a map pin.

The rule that came out of it: short forms are TRUNCATIONS, never substitutions, and never lifted from a 'hidden' register name. The register carries orca / humpback / elephant seal / bottlenose dolphin / right whale dolphin as hidden rows — evidence a string is in use, explicitly not one it offers for display. So an unattributed killer whale reads 'Killer whale', not 'Orca'. Recorded in 029's Implementation notes.

title: animals: add birder alpha codes OSPR, HOSP, UNBI
description:
Filed salish-sea/animals#25 on 2026-08-14. Verified against the IBP alpha code list by extracting the PDF, not from memory.

Add as hidden names under a new IBP source (authority, not use — unlike ORCASOUND, which only claims a name is in use):
- SSA:0000907 Aves -> UNBI ("Unidentified Bird", Aves (gen, sp) — rank matches exactly)
- SSA:0000910 Pandion haliaetus -> OSPR
- SSA:0000911 Passer domesticus -> HOSP

SSA:0000909 Cepphus columba already has PIGU; the list confirms it.

DO NOT add UNLG to SSA:0000908 Laridae. UNLG is "Unidentified Larus Gull" — Larus is a GENUS, Laridae is a FAMILY that also holds terns and kittiwakes. Attaching it narrows the entity through a name, passes validation, and is the ADR-0019 guarantee's failure mode arriving by a route the guarantee does not cover (a curator adding a name at the wrong rank, not a fold collision). Recorded in the issue so it is not "fixed" later.

Open: license status for the IBP source needs deciding rather than assuming cleared. Six-letter scientific codes (PANHAL, PASDOM, AVEGSP, CEPCOL) exist as a second system; not proposed, no evidence of use.

Low value until OrcaHello's tag corpus is actually read — its api/tags endpoint is [AllowAnonymous] but the host is unknown.
notes: UPDATE 2026-08-19: 'kier' was a typo for 'keir', fixed in orcahello#573 — the earlier IBP search only ruled out KI__ codes, not KE__. dthaler says KEIR and PIGU are both 4-letter birder codes (the system Dave Bain uses for birds). Before the register carries KEIR: verify it against the IBP alpha code list and identify the species — if it checks out, extend animals#25 to add it the same way as PIGU/OSPR/HOSP/UNBI. Tracked in salish-8vr.23.

title: orcasite: JSON:API include emits type: null for tags
description: Filed orcasound/orcasite#1011 2026-08-13. Tag and ItemTag lack the AshJsonApi.Resource extension and a json_api type block, so included tags serialize with type: null; feed, which has both, is correct. Blocks nothing on our side — we can key on the relationship name — but a typed include is what lets a generic JSON:API client walk the graph. Watch for a fix; no work here.
close_reason: Fixed upstream and deployed to staging 2026-08-14; orcasound/orcasite#1011 closed as completed.

title: Upload the branded social preview to GitHub repo settings
description: GitHub exposes no REST or GraphQL endpoint for a repository's social preview image, so docs/branding/github-social-preview.png (1280x640, built by scripts/branding/build-icons.sh) has to be uploaded by hand at Settings -> General -> Social preview. Until then the repo card is GitHub's auto-generated tile. Blocked on PR #390 landing the file. Repeat this after any brand change: the build regenerates the file, but GitHub keeps serving the last upload.

title: Backfill ORCIDs for existing iNaturalist contributors
description:
20260621010000_inat_orcid_capture.sql is forward-only by construction: it says so plainly — the 3,072 existing iNat contributor rows are not backfilled because inaturalist.observations does not retain the raw user JSON and the upsert's WHEN MATCHED branch does not re-mint (D-16). So re-ingest will never cover them; only contributors who post a NEW observation get an ORCID.

Needs a one-time pass over the iNat users API keyed on contributors.inat_login, writing through a path that respects the new canonical-URI CHECK.

Note this does not by itself put an ORCID in the archive: iNat records are excluded by SRC-01, and iNat contributor rows are separate from native ones. Its value is the register of identities, plus whatever cross-provider resolution later does with it.
acceptance_criteria: Existing iNat contributors with a linked ORCID have it stored; the pass is idempotent and re-runnable.

title: Validate the contributors_orcid_is_canonical_uri constraint
description:
The CHECK added in 20260813200000_dwc_recorded_by_id.sql is NOT VALID: it governs new writes but never audited the ~3,000 existing iNat-sourced rows. Deliberate — a constraint failure there would have failed the deploy carrying it, since the deploy job runs supabase db push before flipping the frontend.

Audit and finish it: SELECT count(*) FROM public.contributors WHERE orcid IS NOT NULL AND orcid !~ '^https://orcid\\.org/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3}[0-9X]$'; then either ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT (if clean) or normalise the offenders first. Run against prod, not just local — the iNat rows are a prod-only population.
acceptance_criteria: Constraint is VALIDATED in prod, or the non-conforming rows are documented and normalised.
notes:
Pre-audited 2026-08-13 before deployment: all 46 non-NULL prod orcid values were run through public.is_valid_orcid and passed both shape and ISO 7064 check digit, predicting a clean validation.

Closed legitimately the same day: ALTER TABLE public.contributors VALIDATE CONSTRAINT was actually run against prod after a43d8a5 deployed the constraint, and pg_constraint.convalidated is now true — the whole existing population scanned and passed, as predicted.

An earlier close reason on this issue wrongly implied deployment alone finished it. Deploying a NOT VALID constraint does not validate it; that is a separate statement.
close_reason: Pre-empted: the constraint and public.is_valid_orcid deployed to prod with a43d8a5, and the audit run beforehand showed all 46 prod ORCIDs pass shape and check digit. Reopen only if VALIDATE CONSTRAINT is later found not to have been run — see the note below.

title: Track the Bioregistry prefix request for SSA to merge
description:
Filed biopragmatics/bioregistry#2028 on 2026-08-13 requesting prefix 'ssa' (Salish Sea Animals), per animals ADR-0021. Two fields deliberately left blank and flagged in the request: no URI format (the register is a publication, not a service — ADR-0014) and no data license (unresolved; animals Q24/#15 is whether releasing republishes the Bigg's sheet).

Watch for curator questions. If they require a resolver or a license, that is a decision for the animals repo, not something to answer ad hoc in the thread. Once merged, the entry should appear at https://bioregistry.io/ssa — update animals ADR-0021 from 'being registered' to registered, with the entry URL.

title: animals: point ADR-0018's open question at salishsea-io decision 028
description: animals ADR-0018 closes with 'Does OrcaSound get a written recommendation, and from which repository?' That is now answered: salishsea-io decision 028 makes this repository the single voice. Update ADR-0018 (still Proposed) to cite 028 and close the question, so the register does not re-open it.

title: Haul-out clustering for pinnipeds (GH #385)
description:
Spatial aggregation of repeated pinniped sightings at fixed haul-out sites — the pinniped-shaped analogue of a travel segment. Public issue: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/issues/385

Context: travel segments are species-gated by design (decision 027) because pinnipeds are too numerous and not individually identifiable for a travel chain to mean anything. Haul-out clustering is the pattern that DOES apply: seals return to fixed sites, so repeated sightings are evidence about a place, not a journey. ~13,800 pinniped + ~1,600 otter occurrences currently aggregate into nothing.

Design questions are open — see the GitHub issue. A harbor-seal catalog with photo-ID would separately make the taxon eligible for real segments; that is not this work.

title: Replace reconstructed brand assets with Liam's source exports
description: PR #381 ships assets reconstructed from preview PNGs on #286: favicon geometry, teal-mark header lockup recolor, light-background wordmark recolor, social-card composition. When Liam adds source exports to the Drive folder (mark-only SVGs, light-background lockup, pattern tile, typeface name — requested in the #286 comment), swap the reconstructions for his files: public/favicon.svg, public/favicon.ico, public/apple-touch-icon.png, public/social-card.jpg, src/assets/lockup-dark.svg.
close_reason: Done in 2881d81 on branding-286. All five outputs now derive from Liam's exports, checked in under docs/branding/source and built by scripts/branding/build-icons.sh. lockup-dark.svg needed no change — the improvised teal recolor was byte-identical to his teal-mark colorway. Typeface recorded: DIN Alternate Bold, tracking -50.

title: orcanode-monitor: inference lag raises no event
description: Model processing lag is dashboard-only. OrcanodeEventTypes covers HydrophoneStream, MezmoLogging, DataplicityConnection, SocketXPConnection, SDCardSize; InferenceSystemFetcher never calls AddOrcanodeEvent. So a stream outage notifies via the IFTTT trigger API but a model silently falling behind (or a pod flapping) only changes a cell colour on a page somebody has to be looking at. Looks like a gap rather than a decision: add an inference-lag event type raised on the same status-transition pattern the other fetchers use. Files: OrcanodeMonitor/Core/InferenceSystemFetcher.cs, OrcanodeMonitor/Models/OrcanodeEvent.cs:169

title: guard.test.ts row-floor test is vacuous in CI and fails locally
description:
scripts/dwca/guard.test.ts:203 sets process.env.ROW_FLOOR='9999999999' inside the test body, but scripts/dwca/guard.ts:41 evaluates ROW_FLOOR at module import time (`const ROW_FLOOR = BigInt(process.env['ROW_FLOOR'] ?? 1000)`). The override therefore never takes effect and the guard runs against the default floor of 1000.

In CI the test still passes, but for the wrong reason: supabase/ci-seed.sql seeds only a handful of occurrences, so the real row count is already below the default floor. The assertion never exercises what it claims to. On a developer machine with a realistically populated local dwc schema (27,391 rows here) the guard does not trip and the test fails.

Found while verifying the pnpm migration (salish-w3y) — NOT caused by it; reproduces identically under npm.
design: Options: (a) inject the floors as parameters/an options object into main() rather than reading module-level env, which is the honest fix and makes the other floor tests non-vacuous too; (b) vi.resetModules() + dynamic re-import after setting env; (c) vi.stubEnv before import. (a) is preferred — the same import-time-const pattern applies to ZIP_FLOOR_BYTES and PARQUET_FLOOR_BYTES, whose tests only pass because they mock fs.stat rather than needing an env override.
acceptance_criteria: The row-floor test fails if the guard's row check is removed (mutation-tested), and passes against both a seeded CI database and a fully populated local one.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #375 (754c4e9), merged 2026-08-04. main() now takes injectable GuardFloors defaulting to floorsFromEnv(), evaluated per call rather than at import. Also rejects floors that would disable the guard (Number('')===0 from an unset workflow var would have silently passed an empty archive) and stops the nightly's failure issue misreporting a config rejection as 'failed before guard.ts could run'. 356 -> 378 tests; mutation-tested with no DSN set, where the old suite caught nothing. Reviewed by CodeRabbit (CLI x3 + PR-side) and an independent Fable pass; each layer found a distinct instance of the same underlying flaw (coverage that only looks real because ambient values line up).

title: Reconcile the two remaining prod/migration drifts and drop the pull-prod-db.sh workarounds
description:
Two schema drifts found in the salish-0ew sweep (2026-07-30) were recorded but never fixed or explicitly accepted. Both are still worked around in scripts/pull-prod-db.sh, so a prod mirror succeeds while the underlying drift persists.

1. **happywhale.encounter_sample exists only in prod.** One `id integer` column, 5,610 rows, referenced nowhere in the repo — an ad-hoc sampling leftover. Either drop it in prod or add a migration. pull-prod-db.sh excludes it (`-x happywhale.encounter_sample`, line 94).

2. **happywhale.individuals.primary_id and .nickname are varchar(100) in prod; migrations declare varchar(50).** Only nickname needs the width (2 rows over 50 chars, max 60); primary_id maxes at 28. pull-prod-db.sh widens nickname locally so the load succeeds (line 116).

title: Retire or replace the last in-DB HTTP functions (HappyWhale)
description:
Three in-database functions still make live HTTP calls from Postgres:

- `happywhale.fetch_species_config`
- `happywhale.ensure_species`
- `happywhale.ensure_inat_taxa`

They are the last of the pattern decision 011 set out to remove — Postgres keeps storage and pure relational views, ingest lives in a TypeScript imperative shell.

## Why they were left behind

Migration `20260731120000` retired the equivalent Maplify and iNaturalist functions (salish-89d.3). These were deliberately not included, because HappyWhale was **never part of that cutover**:

- `ingest.runs` has no `happywhale` rows at all — 7,053 iNaturalist runs and 7,091 Maplify runs, zero HappyWhale.
- No cron job has ever scheduled them.
- There is no TypeScript replacement to move the work to.

So dropping them would remove the only mechanism, dormant as it is, with nothing standing behind it. That is a different decision from retiring a path that has a proven replacement running in production, and it belongs in its own change.

Prod does hold HappyWhale data (~5,600 encounters, ~176 kB of individuals), so it was populated at some point — presumably by hand. Whether that data is still wanted, and whether it should be refreshed at all, is the actual question here.

## What to decide first

1. **Is HappyWhale still a source we want?** Check `docs/data-provenance.md` and the rights position before building anything. If the answer is no, this is a deletion, not a migration.
2. If yes, port the fetch into `supabase/functions/ingest` alongside `fetch-maplify.ts` and `fetch-inaturalist.ts`, give it an `ingest.runs` source, and only then drop the three functions.
3. Either way, `supabase/seed.sql` no longer calls `fetch_species_config` — nothing depends on these today.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded on whether HappyWhale remains a source.
- If retained: the fetch lives in supabase/functions/ingest, writes an ingest.runs row, and is scheduled the same way Maplify and iNaturalist are.
- The three happywhale.* HTTP functions are dropped in a migration.
- No function in any schema makes an outbound HTTP call from Postgres.

title: Integrate Flukebook (Wildbook) for computer-vision individual identification
description:
WHY: Photo-ID by eye doesn't scale. Flukebook — the Wildbook-based CV photo-ID platform for whales/dolphins — can match a sighting's photos to known individuals automatically, turning every photographed occurrence into a candidate identification. A differentiating, 'killer' feature.

WHAT: Submit occurrence photos to Flukebook's matching API; receive ranked candidate individual matches with confidence scores; record them as candidate Identifications against public.individuals. Flukebook individual IDs map to our catalog as an external-catalog link (alongside HappyWhale). CV match scores are a natural input to the validation model (salish-ek3): high-confidence matches may auto-validate, others stay candidate for human review.

SPIKE / OPEN QUESTIONS (resolve before build):
- Wildbook/Flukebook API capabilities: species coverage (SRKW, Bigg's/transients, humpback), submission + async match-result model, auth, rate/cost.
- Two-way? Whether we also contribute photos/encounters back to Flukebook.
- Cross-catalog dedup: HappyWhale is already mirrored; avoid representing the same animal as two unlinked catalog individuals.

DEPENDS ON the individuals catalog; produces candidate Identifications that feed the identification + validation model.
design:
Two viable architectures (research: docs/research/flukebook-wildbook-api.md):
(A) Contribute INTO hosted Flukebook — request a free account, push encounters/photos via web submit or spreadsheet Bulk Import, let Flukebook's pipeline match, read results back via the login-gated read-only /rest/ query API (what RWildbook wraps). No public 'POST photo → poll for match JSON' endpoint exists on flukebook.org; write access + results at that level need a data-sharing conversation with Wild Me / Conservation X Labs. Data model: 'all data rights remain with contributor' (no CC auto-licensing).
(B) Self-host Wildbook + WBIA (both AGPL) and call WBIA's async job engine directly (/api/engine/query/..., jobid + poll/callback). Full CV control; ops + infra cost.
Either way the match model is async (queue/poll), never request/response.
acceptance_criteria: Photographed occurrences receive ranked candidate individual matches from Flukebook, recorded as candidate identifications with source + confidence score, mapped to public.individuals via a Flukebook external-catalog link.
notes: PARKED 2026-07-03: research complete (docs/research/flukebook-wildbook-api.md), but actual integration is significant product work — not being pursued now. Dominant next action when picked up is a single Wild Me / CXL conversation (orca accuracy + v4 access/licensing + integration path); a draft outreach exists in session history. Deprioritized P2→P3 to match the rest of the individuals epic as unscheduled future work.
